spans.title: Snails and Suspicions
spans.blurb: Over snails and oysters, two friends weigh whether suspicion is ever a duty, until the doctor at the next table breaks in with a grievance of his own.

spans.title: The Priest's Confession
spans.blurb: Pressed at last to explain how he untangles murders, a small quiet priest gives an answer that lifts his questioner clean out of his chair.
spans.spoilerNote: Gives away the titular 'secret' of the priest's method, which the book's frame story stages as its own reveal.

spans.title: Shots in the Judge's Garden
spans.blurb: On a midnight ramble, a detective and his friend hear two revolver shots from a judge's strangely illuminated garden and go over the wall.

books.pairNote: The confession frame and the garden murder come from different parts of the book and share no text or payoff.

spans.title: The City in the Ice
spans.blurb: Two explorers in a small aeroplane climb toward an untrodden polar pass, where the wind pipes weirdly through cave mouths, and look on what no human eye has seen.
spans.spoilerNote: Reveals that the mirage city beyond the mountains is real, one of the book's staged discoveries, though none of its deeper horrors.

spans.title: A Hard Man's Daughter
spans.blurb: A millionaire confronts the son-in-law who ruined his daughter's marriage, and hears a colder account of that marriage than he bargained for.

spans.title: Close to the Front
spans.blurb: On a garden bench near the front, a soldier admires a nurse's hair, and she tells him, without tears, exactly what the war has already taken from her.

spans.title: The Dugout
spans.blurb: In a shallow dugout, ambulance drivers share macaroni, cheese, and sour wine while the shelling walks closer with every cough of the guns.

books.pairNote: A first meeting and a wounding, far apart in the book, with no shared text and neither spoiling the other.

spans.title: They Needn't Die in My House
spans.blurb: A gentle peer, newly restored to his ancestral acres, complains about steam-roller personalities, depressing virtues, and the sheer inconsiderateness of people dying in his house.

spans.title: The Man in the Road
spans.blurb: A fast car, a man reeling out of the hedge, a dying message she cannot understand: then the doctor comes back from his surgery looking grim.
spans.spoilerNote: Reveals an early death and the dying message that launches the book's plot, though none of its later secrets.

books.pairNote: Comic banter at the house and a death on the road; separate scenes in different registers.

spans.title: Tea with Mr. Gilder
spans.blurb: Her brother invents an errand and vanishes, leaving her alone in a gray-eyed stranger's library, where the hospitality turns out to have a purpose.
spans.spoilerNote: Hints that the heroine's heart turns toward Dick rather than her fiance, and that her brother is in Gilder's power, early developments rather than final reveals.

spans.title: The Man with the Guitar
spans.blurb: A merry Italian stranger fills the kitchen with song and chatter, until the narrator's father holds out his hand for the guitar he has itched to play for years.

spans.title: A Tapping at the Window
spans.blurb: Safe by the fire in a lonely hut, a boy listens to his father's tale of buried gold and dead men, until something taps at the window.

books.pairNote: The guitar visitor and the fireside tale are separate episodes with no shared text.

spans.title: Ten Thousand Pounds
spans.blurb: A hospital doctor, desperate for funds, takes a telephone call from a young woman who claims she has already sent him ten thousand pounds, after a fashion.

spans.title: The Midnight Ambulance
spans.blurb: While a great house sleeps, a slim figure slips from bedroom to bedroom among the guests' jewels, and an ambulance idles at the door below.

books.pairNote: Two separate capers by the same thief; each carries its own payoff.

spans.title: Another Man's Face
spans.blurb: An old woman holds up the candle and looks from one young man to the other: the same face twice, and only one of them owns it.
spans.spoilerNote: Reveals that the villainous usher has an exact double, machinery the book later puts to use.

spans.title: Making a Swing
spans.blurb: At midnight a schoolmaster knots three ropes together and climbs from his window, telling the feverish boy in his care that he is making a swing.

books.pairNote: The double's unveiling and the night crime are different scenes; neither gives away the other's punch.
